newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel sets 15 bln yen samurai issue for July 23.
newsitem.headline: Israel sets 15 bln yen samurai issue for July 23.

text.p: Israel will make a 15 billion yen ($130 million) samurai bond offering in Japan on July 23, Israel's Treasury said on Wednesday.

The offering, Israel's first in the samurai market, will be for 10-year bonds, the longest term ever by a first-time issuer in the market. The amount is at the low end of earlier Treasury estimates of 15-20 billion yen for the size of the offering.

The chief underwriter is Daiwa Securities Co, which replaced Nomura Securities Co last month. In addition, Yamaichi Securities Co, Nikko Securities Co, Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan (LTCB), Kokusai Securities Co and Morgan Stanley Tokyo will serve as co-managers.
The Treasury said that both Moody's and Standard and Poor's had re-affirmed Israel's credit rating. The bonds will be rated A-minus, the same as those issued overseas in 1995 and 1996.
The Treasury said accountant-general Shy Talmon will be going to Japan for the roadshow.

The offering was originally scheduled to take place in early June before Japan's securities watchdog opened an investigation into allegations that Nomura had illegal dealings with corporate racketeers.
Israel delayed the offering in the wake of the news and later gave the mandate to underwrite the issue to Daiwa.
The issue is one of a series the Israeli government is making to test overseas markets before the U.S. loan guarantees it has been borrowing against expire at the end of next year.
Israel has already made offerings in the Euro- and Yankee bond markets.
